speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower what enforcement powers does the Ministry deploy when investigating referrals from TAFEP about employers who may be engaging in discriminatory HR practices that are not related to nationality but to other attributes, such as age and gender.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and the Tripartite Partners also expect employers to implement fair and non-discriminatory employment practices in accordance with the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (TAFEP).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This is why TAFEP, as the advocate and champion for fair employment practices, takes an active role in looking into complaints of such unfair employment practices and refers cases to MOM for enforcement, if found to be true.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Any employee who feels discriminated against can approach TAFEP for assistance.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In such cases, what were the tools of enforcement used?

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: So far, we have received complaints of other attributes besides nationality, age and gender.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We have received complaints based on attributes, such as race, language, religion, family status and others.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Most of the time, we will investigate, gather the evidence and I am encouraged that most of the companies rectified their employment practices.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We are monitoring the situation and will work with TAFEP closely.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Whenever there is a complaint and a need to investigate, we will do so.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: What we will do is to continue to educate and create greater awareness.
